name: combo-box
title: ComboBox
description: The sheet has no combobox class of its own — it is the search affix and the select menu put together, which is what a combobox is: a text field that filters a list as you type, where the list is the value rather than a hint about it.

files.content: import { useContext } from 'react' import { Autocomplete as AriaAutocomplete, AutocompleteStateContext, Button as AriaButton, FieldError as AriaFieldError, Header as AriaHeader, Label as AriaLabel, ListBox as AriaListBox, ListBoxItem as AriaListBoxItem, ListBoxSection as AriaListBoxSection, Popover as AriaPopover, Select as AriaSelect, SelectStateContext, SelectValue as AriaSelectValue, Text as AriaText, } from 'react-aria-components' import type { ButtonProps as AriaButtonProps, FieldErrorProps as AriaFieldErrorProps, HeaderProps as AriaHeaderProps, LabelProps as AriaLabelProps, ListBoxItemProps as AriaListBoxItemProps, AutocompleteProps as AriaAutocompleteProps, ListBoxProps as AriaListBoxProps, ListBoxSectionProps as AriaListBoxSectionProps, PopoverProps as AriaPopoverProps, SelectProps as AriaSelectProps, SelectValueProps as AriaSelectValueProps, TextProps as AriaTextProps, } from 'react-aria-components' import { ERROR, FIELD, FIELD_SIZES, HINT, LABEL } from '../field' import type { FieldSize } from '../field' import { SearchField } from '../SearchField/SearchField' /** * The sheet's `.ds-select-btn`. * * It is the same control as `.ds-input` — the same height, the same fill, the same * resting hairline and the same focus treatment — so it reads `--field-border` and * `--field-hover` from the field root rather than deciding either itself. That is what * makes a field and a select sit together in a column without a seam. */ const TRIGGER = [ 'flex w-full items-center gap-3', 'h-(--field-control-h) ps-3.5 pe-3.5 text-left', 'border border-(--field-border) bg-muted text-foreground', 'cursor-pointer rounded-none', 'transition-[border-color,background-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse', 'data-[hovered]:not-data-[focused]:border-(--field-hover)', // The sheet turns the border teal on focus and leaves the UA ring off; Chrome gives a // focused button `outline-style: auto` regardless, so it has to be said explicitly. 'data-[focused]:outline-none', 'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40', ].join(' ') /** * The sheet's `.placeholder` — 35%, the same weight as an input's placeholder. The * state is on the value itself, so this needs no group. */ const VALUE = 'min-w-0 flex-1 truncate data-[placeholder]:text-foreground/35' /** * The rest of a multiple selection, counted rather than listed. * * Showing every chosen name is what a native multi-select does, and it fails the moment the * list outgrows the trigger: the value truncates and the ellipsis eats the one fact the * trigger is for — how many things are selected. Naming the first and counting the rest keeps * both, and the count is `shrink-0`, so it can never be the part that gets cut. */ const COUNT = [ 'ms-2 shrink-0 align-middle', 'bg-foreground/8 px-1.5 py-0.5 font-mono text-[11px] text-foreground/70', ].join(' ') /** * The sheet puts `.ds-caret` 14px from the right, at half height. The icon is absolutely * positioned and the trigger keeps its `pe-10`, so replacing the caret with a spinner — * which is a different size — cannot shift the value beside it. */ const ICON = 'flex size-3 shrink-0 items-center justify-center' /** * The box is a fixed 12x12 in the flow, so swapping the 10x6 caret for the 12px spinner * cannot shift the value beside it. Alignment is the trigger's flex, not an absolute * offset, which is what lets it be a normal flex child. * * The rotation stays the standalone `rotate` property rather than a `transform`, which is * why the sheet can write it independently — and why it can be driven by a variable set * on the root, where `data-open` lives. */ const ICON_CARET = [ ICON, 'rotate-(--dropdown-caret-rotate) [color:var(--dropdown-caret-ink)]', 'transition-[rotate,color] duration-[160ms] ease-pulse', ].join(' ') /** Same box, no rotation: a spinner that turned when the menu opened would read as a fault. */ const ICON_SPINNER = [ICON, '[color:var(--dropdown-caret-ink)]'].join(' ') /** * The sheet's `.ds-select-menu`. The border and shadow sit on the popover, because that * is the positioned box; the scrolling sits on the list inside it, so the options move * under a fixed frame rather than dragging the frame's edges with them. */ const MENU = [ 'flex w-(--trigger-width) flex-col overflow-hidden', 'border border-border-strong bg-card', 'shadow-[0_12px_32px_rgba(0,0,0,.7)]', ].join(' ') const LIST = 'max-h-[264px] overflow-auto p-0 outline-none' /** The sheet's `.ds-select-option`: 13px, 75%, with the accent reserved for the choice. */ const OPTION = [ 'flex items-center justify-between gap-3', 'px-3.5 py-[11px] text-[13px] text-foreground/75', 'cursor-pointer select-none', 'data-[hovered]:bg-foreground/7 data-[hovered]:text-foreground', 'data-[focus-visible]:outline-none data-[focus-visible]:bg-foreground/7 data-[focus-visible]:text-foreground', 'data-[selected]:text-primary', ].join(' ') const OPTION_LABEL = 'truncate' /** * The sheet marks the chosen option with a literal `[SET]` rather than a tick — its own * idiom, kept as-is. It is `aria-hidden` because `aria-selected` already says this, and * a screen reader announcing "set" on top of "selected" would be noise. */ const MARKER = 'shrink-0 font-mono text-[11px] text-warning data-[slot=marker]:select-none' /** The sheet's `.ds-select-group-label`. */ const GROUP_LABEL = [ 'px-3.5 pt-[9px] pb-1', 'text-[11px] uppercase tracking-[0.08em] text-foreground/45', ].join(' ') const SECTION = 'flex flex-col' /** * The search sits above the options behind the same hairline the menu is drawn with, so * it reads as part of the surface rather than as a field dropped into it. */ const SEARCH = 'border-b border-border-strong p-2' /** * A select does **not** mark itself invalid with `aria-invalid`, and that is correct * rather than a gap. Its trigger is a `

/**
 * The field anatomy, shared by every control that wears it — `TextField`,
 * `SearchField`, and the textarea, select, checkbox and radio still to come.
 *
 * Only the styling lives here. Each component defines its own slot components,
 * thin as they are, so that its docs and manifest describe its own API rather
 * than pointing at another component's.
 */

/**
 * The three control sizes. `size` is set once on the field and travels as two
 * custom properties rather than through React context: the control, and any
 * affix inside it, are ordinary descendants of the field, so inheritance already
 * does the work. It also means a one-off override is just a utility on the
 * element rather than a new prop.
 */
export type FieldSize = 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg'

export const FIELD_SIZES: Record<FieldSize, string> = {
  sm: '[--field-control-h:2.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.8125rem]', // 36px / 13px
  md: '[--field-control-h:2.75rem] [--field-control-text:0.875rem]', // 44px / 14px
  lg: '[--field-control-h:3.25rem] [--field-control-text:0.9375rem]', // 52px / 15px
}

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field`: legend, control, then the hint that explains it.
 *
 * The `font-size` here is what the control and any affix inherit. It sits on the
 * field rather than on the input so it still reaches an affix, which is the
 * input's sibling — a `cap`-sized icon would otherwise match the page's font
 * instead of the field's.
 *
 * The two border properties are published here for the same reason `Checkbox`
 * publishes its own: read-only lives on the field root, while the border it changes
 * is on the input, and a group variant cannot win that cascade — see the note on
 * `INPUT`. Declaring them here means the input only reads them, and the ordinary
 * cascade decides, because `[data-readonly]` plainly outranks the bare declaration.
 */
export const FIELD = [
  'group flex flex-col gap-2 [font-size:var(--field-control-text)]',
  '[--field-border:var(--color-input)]',
  '[--field-hover:var(--color-border)]',
  // Read-only is not disabled: the value is the whole point of the field, so it
  // keeps full-strength text. Only the affordances go — a quieter hairline, and no
  // brightening on hover — because there is nothing here to invite a click on.
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-border:var(--color-border-soft)]',
  'data-[readonly]:[--field-hover:var(--color-border-soft)]',
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix` wrapper. `Group` exists for one case: an affix is
 * positioned against the control, but the field also holds the legend and the
 * hint, so an affix anchored to the field would centre on all three.
 * Wrapping the control gives the affix the right box — and it stays opt-in, so a
 * plain field has no extra element at all.
 *
 * The two `:has()` rules are here for the same reason: the room an affix needs is
 * padding on the input, and the group is what can see both of them. The input
 * itself never has to know it has neighbours.
 */
export const GROUP = [
  'relative flex w-full',
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-start]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:ps-10.5', // 42px, per the sheet's search field
  'has-[[data-slot=icon-end]]:[&>[data-slot=input]]:pe-14', // 56px, per the sheet's trailing unit
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`: 12px, uppercase, letterspaced, white 70%.
 *
 * The required marker is drawn from the field's own `data-required`, so the label
 * never has to be told and the asterisk cannot drift out of sync with
 * `isRequired`. The input already carries the native `required`, so this is the
 * visual half of the same fact.
 */
export const LABEL = [
  'text-[12px] uppercase tracking-[0.04em] text-muted-foreground',
  "group-data-[required]:after:ms-1 group-data-[required]:after:text-destructive group-data-[required]:after:content-['*']",
].join(' ')

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-input`.
 *
 * The resting hairline is what identifies the control. The sheet gives
 * `.ds-input` a transparent border and leaves the panel-2 fill to do the job, but
 * that fill is 1.23:1 on the dark page and 1.17:1 on the light one, so the field is
 * nearly invisible as a boundary in both. `--input` is the smallest
 * hairline that clears the 3:1 a control boundary needs on each.
 *
 * Hover has to *strengthen* it rather than replace it: the sheet's hover is white
 * at 25%, which is now weaker than the resting line and would erase it.
 *
 * `outline-none` on focus suppresses the *browser's* ring, which is what the
 * sheet's `.ds-input:focus { outline: none }` is really doing. Chrome gives a
 * focused text input its `:focus-visible` ring at `outline-style: auto` regardless
 * of React Aria's attribute, so leaving it alone means a blue UA ring on a teal
 * system. Focus is then the border alone — adding the shared 3px-offset ring here
 * would draw two parallel teal hairlines with a gap, which reads as a fault.
 * `Button` can carry that ring because the edge it repeats is a solid fill.
 */
export const INPUT = [
  'w-full font-mono rounded-none border border-(--field-border)',
  'h-(--field-control-h) px-3.5',
  'bg-muted text-foreground placeholder:text-foreground/35',
  'transition-[border-color,background-color] duration-[120ms] ease-pulse',
  // Focus and invalid stay literal, so they outrank the published border and always
  // win — including on a read-only field, which is still focusable and still the
  // field the caret should be able to reach.
  'data-[hovered]:not-data-[focused]:border-(--field-hover)',
  'data-[focused]:outline-none data-[focused]:border-primary',
  'data-[invalid]:not-data-[focused]:border-destructive',
  'data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed data-[disabled]:opacity-40',
  // Read-only gets the cursor and nothing else that dims it. `opacity` here would
  // take the *value* down with it — at 40% the text measures 3.42:1, under the 4.5:1
  // body text needs, so the one thing the user came to read becomes the thing they
  // cannot.
  'group-data-[readonly]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet's `.ds-hint`: 12px, tighter tracking, white 55%. */
export const HINT = 'text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-foreground/55'

/**
 * The sheet paints its error state yellow, because the original design had only
 * two accents and yellow was the nearest thing to a warning it owned. That does
 * not carry over here: `--warning` is this system's `secondary` button, so
 * errors would be the same colour as a secondary action. The error state uses
 * `--destructive`, the danger hue, and keeps the sheet's flex so an icon can be
 * dropped in front of the message.
 */
export const ERROR =
  'flex items-center gap-1.5 text-[12px] tracking-[-0.5px] text-destructive'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-affix__unit` and `.ds-affix__icon`: pinned to the control's
 * box, vertically centred, and never a click target — the affix is decoration, and
 * a pointer-events-owning overlay would swallow clicks meant for the field. Sized
 * in `cap` like `Button.Icon`, so one icon works at every field `size`.
 */
export const ICON = [
  'absolute inset-y-0 z-10 grid place-items-center pointer-events-none',
  'text-foreground/70',
  '[&>svg]:block [&>svg]:h-[1.5cap] [&>svg]:w-auto [&>svg]:shrink-0',
].join(' ')

/** The sheet insets both affixes 14px from their edge. */
export const ICON_POSITIONS = {
  start: 'start-3.5',
  end: 'end-3.5',
} as const

export type IconPosition = keyof typeof ICON_POSITIONS

/**
 * The recipes a list of options shares — `ListBox`, the `Select` and `ComboBox` menus, and the `Menu`.
 *
 * Extracted rather than copied, for the reason `field.ts`, `date.tsx` and `loadMore.tsx` exist: an option
 * that looks one way in a select and another way in a standalone list is one component wearing two
 * designs.
 */

/** The scrolling list itself. `p-0` because padding belongs to the option, so a hovered row reaches the edge. */
export const OPTION_LIST = 'max-h-[264px] overflow-auto p-0'

/**
 * The sheet's `.ds-select-option`: 13px at 75%, with the accent reserved for the choice.
 *
 * **`data-[focus-visible]:outline-none` here is deliberate, and is not the bug `Table` and `GridList`
 * had.** Those declared a ring and then disabled it; this option conveys focus with a **background**
 * instead — the way a menu row does — so there is no ring to disable. Its sibling rule below is what
 * actually paints focus.
 */
export const OPTION = [
  'flex items-center justify-between gap-3',
  'px-3.5 py-[11px] text-[13px] text-foreground/75',
  'cursor-pointer select-none',
  'data-[hovered]:bg-foreground/7 data-[hovered]:text-foreground',
  'data-[focus-visible]:outline-none data-[focus-visible]:bg-foreground/7 data-[focus-visible]:text-foreground',
  'data-[selected]:text-primary',
  // **Disabled dims and does not recolour**, the house rule every other control follows. This was missing
  // until `ListBox`'s own test asserted the opacity of a disabled option and got 1: an option that cannot
  // be chosen looked exactly like one that can, in this list and in the select, combo box and menu above
  // it, which all share this recipe.
  'data-[disabled]:opacity-30 data-[disabled]:cursor-not-allowed',
].join(' ')

docs:
The sheet has no combobox class of its own — it is the search affix and the select menu put
together, which is what a combobox is: a text field that filters a list as you type, where the
list _is_ the value rather than a hint about it.

```tsx
<ComboBox defaultSelectedKey="iad">
  <ComboBox.Label>Monitor</ComboBox.Label>
  <ComboBox.Group>
    <ComboBox.Icon />
    <ComboBox.Input placeholder="Search monitors…" />
    <ComboBox.Button />
  </ComboBox.Group>
  <ComboBox.Popover>
    <ComboBox.OptionList>
      <ComboBox.Option id="fra">fra1 · Frankfurt</ComboBox.Option>
      <ComboBox.Option id="iad">iad1 · Virginia</ComboBox.Option>
    </ComboBox.OptionList>
  </ComboBox.Popover>
  <ComboBox.Hint>One monitor per check.</ComboBox.Hint>
  <ComboBox.Error>Pick a monitor.</ComboBox.Error>
</ComboBox>
```

| Slot                    | React Aria       | Notes                                                   |
| ----------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ComboBox`              | `ComboBox`       | Owns the value. `size` is `sm \| md \| lg`              |
| `ComboBox.Label`        | `Label`          | The sheet's `.ds-field-legend`                          |
| `ComboBox.Group`        | `Group`          | Leaves room for the affixes                             |
| `ComboBox.Input`        | `Input`          | The control itself, with the field's hairline and focus |
| `ComboBox.Icon`         | —                | An affix at either end; draws the magnifier by default  |
| `ComboBox.Button`       | `Button`         | The chevron. `isLoading` swaps it for the spinner       |
| `ComboBox.Popover`      | `Popover`        | The menu surface                                        |
| `ComboBox.OptionList`   | `ListBox`        | The options; takes `renderEmptyState`                   |
| `ComboBox.Option`       | `ListBoxItem`    | One choice, marked `[SET]` when chosen                  |
| `ComboBox.Section`      | `ListBoxSection` | A run of options, announced as a group                  |
| `ComboBox.SectionTitle` | `Header`         | Its heading, in `.ds-select-group-label`                |
| `ComboBox.Hint`         | `Text`           | `slot="description"`                                    |
| `ComboBox.Error`        | `FieldError`     | Renders nothing while valid                             |

The input is the control, so unlike `Select` there is no separate trigger: the chevron is a
button beside it, and `ComboBox.Icon` is an affix the `Group` makes room for through the same
`has-[[data-slot=…]]` rules a `TextField` uses. The height comes from the shared
`--field-control-h`, so a combobox and a field line up — the `Sizes` story asserts it.

### The built-in filter is not applied either

React Aria documents a filter on its combobox, and on a combobox's own collection it does not
run — the query sits in the input and the list shows every option. **This is the same trap as
`Select`**, found the same way, and it means the rule is about React Aria's collections rather
than about either component: a filter has to be passed explicitly for a filtered collection to
narrow at all.

So `ComboBox` supplies `startsWith` as its default, and `defaultFilter` is there to change
_how_ it narrows rather than to switch it on.

### One prop, two answers, both right

`isInvalid` puts `aria-invalid` on a combobox's input and withholds it from a select's trigger.
That is not an inconsistency: the input's role is `combobox`, which supports the attribute,
while a select's trigger is a `button`, which does not. The `Error` story asserts both.

Worth knowing when writing the empty state: React Aria gives the `renderEmptyState` output the
`option` role, so it is counted by `getAllByRole('option')`. The `Empty` story therefore asserts
that no _monitor_ is offered rather than that the option count is zero.
